Step 1: Identify the direction vectors of both lines.
The direction vector of the first line is \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -9 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\).
The direction vector of the second line is \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -18 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}\).

Step 2: Check if the lines are indeed parallel.
Notice that the second direction vector is a scalar multiple of the first direction vector. Specifically, \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -18 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} = 2 \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -9 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\). This confirms that the lines are parallel.

Step 3: Find a point on each line.
A point on the first line is \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\) (when \(t = 0\)).
A point on the second line is \(\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}\) (when \(u = 0\)).

Step 4: Calculate the vector connecting these two points.
The vector connecting the points \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -10 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}\) is \(\begin{pmatrix} -5 - 3 \\ -3 + 10 \\ 6 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -8 \\ 7 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}\).

Step 5: Use the formula for the distance between two parallel lines.
The distance \(d\) between two parallel lines can be found using the formula:
\[ d = \frac{\| \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} \|}{\| \mathbf{c} \|}, \]
where \(\mathbf{a}\) is the vector connecting a point on each line, \(\mathbf{b}\) is the direction vector of the lines, and \(\mathbf{c}\) is the direction vector of the lines (which is the same for both lines).

Step 6: Compute the cross product \(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\).
\[
\begin{pmatrix} -8 \\ 7 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -9 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ -8 & 7 & 5 \\ 2 & -9 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(7 \cdot -2 - 5 \cdot -9) - \mathbf{j}(-8 \cdot -2 - 5 \cdot 2) + \mathbf{k}(-8 \cdot -9 - 7 \cdot 2)
= \mathbf{i}(-14 + 45) - \mathbf{j}(16 - 10) + \mathbf{k}(72 - 14)
= \begin{pmatrix} 31 \\ -6 \\ 58 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Step 7: Calculate the magnitude of the cross product.
\[
\| \begin{pmatrix} 31 \\ -6 \\ 58 \end{pmatrix} \| = \sqrt{31^2 + (-6)^2 + 58^2} = \sqrt{961 + 36 + 3364} = \sqrt{4361}.
\]

Step 8: Calculate the magnitude of the direction vector.
\[
\| \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -9 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} \| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-9)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 81 + 4} = \sqrt{89}.
\]

Step 9: Compute the distance.
\[
d = \frac{\sqrt{4361}}{\sqrt{89}} = \sqrt{\frac{4361}{89}} = \sqrt{49} = 7.
\]

Final answer: \boxed{7}
